title: Exact recovery from separating samples
statement: Let $n,\ell,m$ be natural numbers, and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ have algebraic degree at most $\ell$ after encoding its inputs and outputs in $\mathbb F_2$. If the $m$ encoded sample inputs distinguish all coefficient families on monomials of degree at most $\ell$, then the low-degree polynomial learner trained on those inputs with labels from $f$ evaluates to the encoded function $f$ on every input.
hypotheses_covered: natural numbers n, ℓ, and m
target function has encoded algebraic degree at most ℓ
sample inputs distinguish all low-degree coefficient families
